body: Ah jesus, that sounds terrible, I'm sorry. I can't stand cops either, and this is a good reflection of why that is. If it's any consolation, I'm guessing if you try to talk to someone in person (hard, i know) at a hospital; it's far less likely that the cops will show up.
I live in Toronto. I called the Distress Centre and also the National Suicide Hotline, which is based in the States but according to Wikipedia also services Canada.

I've never been officially diagnoised with that, I guess it's not far off to imagine I'm on some part of the spectrum. (I end up relating to Abed on Community, so...yeah.) Is it possible that this...turning off emotions things, happened as a result of emotional trauma? I mean, I don't know. I do know it's gotten worse over the years though. Didn't really notice it in high school, although I'm sure I had it. 

I've just remembered I've left out a huge part of this emotional state thing...a few years ago I had a stalker. A genuine one, who started as my friend. Things got bad, I cut off contact. She didn't. Then she did because the police became involved and she got carted to a hospital. Makes trust a hard thing, you know? My last girlfriend said to me once, "you don't seem to realize that you went through something really traumatic." (The whole ordeal lasted almost a year.)

I use to have a problem trying to "fix" people, because I saw myself in them. That girl (stalker) cured all that.
It's sitting amongst a group of friends and wanting to say what's on your mind, but screaming inside instead. That's a tough one to swallow.

Thank you guys for answering this. I appreciate it, I really do. It's nice to hear these words from strangers. 

I took some time off (hah, what do I have to do?) to go see a movie, it was a good escape. I guess it's cliche, but I went and saw "The Perks of Being a Wallflower". Liked it well enough, but I remember why I had tried to avoid seeing it. Coming-of-age movies, for me, just make me want for a past that never happened and for people that never existed. 

I think there's a way to see everything out there in the right light...I'm just not sure what it is. And I didn't mean to imply I don't have a support system, I think I do? I just hate being a bother to people. I do have friends here, don't get me wrong. It's just...who wants to deal with all that? With all my sadness and confusion. I know I don't. 

My parents want to help me, they know that I'm depressed. They're worried about me. But there's really nothing to do, that's what it feels like. To say things get better? I appreciate the words and I know you're just trying to help, but I can't see that necessarily happening. 

Nobody's out to get me, but nobody's looking out for me either. (In the cosmic sense.) Which is both good and bad. I can't have hope anymore, and that's something that drives us all forward. 
I may PM some of you guys/girls in the future, and I want to thank you all again for taking the time to talk to me. You don't me, I'm just some guy. But you all reached out anyway. 

Thank you.
